reason: A denser region of the cold cloud is a plausible starting point for gravitational contraction, as in the first star’s formation.

choice.with: A denser patch of the universe

expectation: This should produce a denser, contracting part of the cloud.

effect: The dense patch concentrated the molecular cloud into a contracting filament; the next step is likely further collapse.
reaction: The contrast with the first stars’ unenriched gas is useful.
reason: Escaping radiation previously helped a gas knot contract by carrying away heat, so it is a plausible next step for the filament.
expectation: The filament should cool and contract further toward a protostar.

effect: The filament instead combined with the cloud’s rotation, producing a rotating collapsing core; radiation was not the next operation.
reaction: The compatibility feedback made the role of rotation clearer.
reason: The core could plausibly interact with several remaining ingredients, so checking its partners will guide the next step.
expectation: The inspection should reveal what can advance the collapsing core toward a young Sun or disk.

effect: The rotating core can combine with either the cold molecular cloud or ice-mantled dust, suggesting separate paths toward the Sun and its disk.
reaction: I’m curious how the two ingredients shape those paths.
reason: More cloud material falling into the rotating core plausibly builds the young Sun.
expectation: The core should gather material and develop toward a protostar.

alternatives.reason: The dust might instead advance the disk goal.

effect: The collapsing core and cloud produced the Sun’s protostar, which shines as infalling material releases energy.
reaction: It is useful to see that the protostar can shine before stable fusion.
reason: The core’s other known partner is ice-mantled dust, making it a promising route toward the disk.
expectation: The rotating material and dust should form or advance a disk around the protostar.

effect: The rotating core and icy dust formed the planet-forming disk, completing the disk goal. The young Sun goal remains.
reaction: The inherited icy dust becoming part of a disk is a satisfying connection.
reason: In the earlier star’s formation, hydrogen helped advance a protostar to sustained fusion; the same pairing is worth trying here.
expectation: The protostar should advance toward a young Sun powered by hydrogen fusion.

effect: The protostar became a contracting young Sun, still powered by accretion and contraction rather than sustained hydrogen fusion.
reaction: I was wrong to expect fusion at this stage; the distinction is useful.
reason: The young Sun is central to the remaining goal, but its next partner is unclear, so checking compatibility should guide the next step.
expectation: The inspection should reveal how to advance the young Sun or illuminate its surroundings.

effect: The young Sun can combine with either escaping radiation or the planet-forming disk; both are possible routes toward the remaining goal.
reaction: I’m curious whether the disk interaction will show the Sun lighting its surroundings.
reason: Combining the young Sun with its surrounding disk directly matches the remaining goal.
expectation: The young Sun should illuminate the surrounding disk.

alternatives.reason: Escaping radiation might instead advance the Sun’s evolution.

effect: The young Sun and disk produced a hot inner disk, showing how heating varies with distance; the Sun goal remains incomplete.
reaction: The connection between distance and which materials stay solid is useful.
reason: Escaping radiation is the young Sun’s other known partner and may advance the remaining goal.
expectation: This should advance the young Sun’s evolution or its light reaching its surroundings.

effect: Escaping radiation and the contracting young Sun produced sunlight, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between the young Sun’s light and that of the earlier massive star was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the contracting young Sun was most worthwhile: it corrected my expectation that its light already came from sustained hydrogen fusion.

leastWorthwhile.text: The attempt to cool the filament with escaping radiation was a false start, although compatibility feedback immediately advanced it through rotation.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the young Sun was still powered by contraction and accretion rather than sustained hydrogen fusion.

arbitrary.text: Combining the young Sun with escaping radiation to create sunlight felt somewhat arbitrary; I chose it because it was the other known compatible partner, rather than from a clear physical inference.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow how the hot inner disk and inherited icy dust develop into planets; the distinctions about heating and stellar energy made this chapter informative.
